summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for hepatitis C cirrhosis, recurrent cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease stage 5, type 2 diabetes, and portal hypertension was admitted for acute kidney injury with a creatinine rise to 5.1. She presented with poor oral intake, recent diarrhea, and fluid retention. She had recently been hospitalized for hypoglycemia, UTI, and kidney dysfunction, during which Lantus was discontinued and she completed a course of ciprofloxacin. On admission, she was started on IV fluids and sodium bicarbonate for hyperkalemia, and continued on torsemide for volume management. A Doppler ultrasound showed cirrhosis and small ascites but patent liver vasculature. She received albumin to support renal perfusion. Her creatinine gradually improved to 3.6 by discharge. She was stabilized on insulin therapy, with plans for endocrinology follow-up, and discharged home with nephrology, transplant, and neurology follow-up arranged.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypoglycemia without coma
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Peptic ulcer, site unspecified, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
